newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian, Ugandan leaders discuss Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian, Ugandan leaders discuss Sudan.

text.p: The presidents of Egypt and Uganda met in Cairo on Friday and discussed the fighting in southern Sudan, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni arrived from Brussels for a two-day visit and went straight into talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Uganda and Egypt have similar views on the Islamist government in Khartoum, which has alienated most of Sudan's neighbours by encouraging dissident groups.

Sudan says the Ugandan army is fighting in the south alongside the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army. Uganda says the Sudanese army is helping the Lord's Resistance Army, a rebel organisation based in northern Uganda.

Uganda on Friday said its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 just inside Uganda, beating back a joint attack by the Sudanese army and the Ugandan rebels. A Sudanese minister of state denied this.
Moussa, asked if the two presidents discussed Sudan's accusations against Uganda, said: "Everything to do with this subject was discussed in their talks."

Museveni and Mubarak also discussed economic relations, including investment and agricultural cooperation, Moussa added. Museveni will have talks with Deputy Prime Minister and Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali.
